# NEAR kit plan (xray side)

Seat: mill. Date: 2026-11-15 (CT). Refs [#1082](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/issues/1082). PR [#1100](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/pull/1100).

This plan follows the working tables in [issue comment 6899635909](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/issues/1082#issuecomment-6899635909). For each row it lines up three points: official NEAR docs, a working file in a #1100 MIT/Apache repo, and the simplest xray kit. Mill owns the Repo file and Kit shape columns. Docs links are cited so the three points sit together; near still owns the official Docs column. Nibbler owns New (X).

Scope: light read only (depth-1 clones, README + LICENSE + the named file). No code is copied into xray. Hackathon code is unaudited reference or base only. Testnet first. No mainnet funds.

Proposed install lines and MCP server names below are not shipped yet. They follow how xray already wires servers, which is called out in the factory recipe.

## Per-layer notes (docs, demo, docs vs code)

### Intents + x402 (Anyfare)

- Official docs: [1Click Swap API](https://docs.near-intents.org/integration/distribution-channels/1click-api/about-1click-api.md), [making a request](https://docs.near-intents.org/integration/distribution-channels/1click-api/quickstart/making-a-request.md) (host `https://1click.chaindefuser.com`, `/v0/tokens`, `/v0/quote`, `/v0/status`). Intents index: [docs.near-intents.org/llms.txt](https://docs.near-intents.org/llms.txt). I did not find a first-party x402 page in [docs.near.org/llms.txt](https://docs.near.org/llms.txt) on this pass.
- 5-minute testnet demo (outline): dry `POST /v0/quote` (`dry: true`) for a small USDC output; show a pass (quote returned) and a fail (bad asset id). Then a local x402 verify/settle against a fake or testnet facilitator — no mainnet cents. Anyfare's own README claims hosted demos spend real mainnet money; the xray demo must not.
- Docs vs code: **partial match.** 1Click host and `/v0/quote` paths match the official quickstart. Anyfare splits Intents (topups) and x402 (payments facilitator) across packages; the working table names one layer. Anyfare is documented as mainnet; the premise is testnet first. x402 itself is not a NEAR docs primitive in the official index I fetched.

### Chain Signatures (HyperNear)

- Official docs: [What are Chain Signatures?](https://docs.near.org/chain-abstraction/chain-signatures.md), [signing transactions](https://docs.near.org/chain-abstraction/chain-signatures/implementation.md).
- 5-minute testnet demo (outline): derive one MPC address from a testnet contract + path; request one `sign` on a dummy payload; pass = signature recovers to the derived address; fail = policy rejects an over-cap call. Do not send funds on Base in the first demo.
- Docs vs code: **disagree on the target chain.** Official docs describe signing on other chains including EVM. This contract signs Hyperliquid L1 actions, not Base / ETH / BTC. "Intents" in this repo are EIP-712 owner intents, not NEAR Intents. Testnet only; mainnet is not deployed. `sign_raw` exists only under a `spike` feature and is not in a default build.

### NEAR AI Cloud / TEE (Abalone)

- Official docs: [private inference](https://docs.near.ai/cloud/private-inference.md), [GET attestation report](https://docs.near.ai/api-reference/attestation/get-attestation-report.md), [inference SDK](https://docs.near.ai/cloud/inference-sdk/index.md), [OpenAI compatibility](https://docs.near.ai/cloud/guides/openai-compatibility.md). Index: [docs.near.ai/llms.txt](https://docs.near.ai/llms.txt).
- 5-minute testnet / cloud demo (outline): `attest_model` against `https://cloud-api.near.ai/v1/attestation/report` for a Confidential TEE model (pass = nonce echoes and report verifies); fail = refuse an Incognito model or a failed quote. One short `complete_verified` after a passing attest. No mainnet payments.
- Docs vs code: **match on the report path, differ on the SDK.** Abalone calls `GET /v1/attestation/report` and `POST /v1/chat/completions` directly (`lib/near.mjs`), not `@nearai/inference-sdk`. Keep the official report path; do not assume the SDK is already used. Carry `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. Confidential vs Incognito must stay labeled (see the 16:54Z scan on #1082).

### OutLayer / TDX (ProvenExit named base)

- Official docs: [OutLayer](https://docs.near.org/primitives/off-chain-compute/outlayer.md) (Rust/WASM in Intel TDX, `request_execution`). TDX attestation for *models* is on the NEAR AI Cloud side, not this page.
- 5-minute testnet demo (outline): read `is_allowed` / a recorded `debug_verify_tdx` against `vpnreg.pe-owner-erhan.testnet` or a local fixture (pass = approved compose hash; fail = revoked hash). A later OutLayer demo would call `request_execution` from Fulfil's trait, not from ProvenExit.
- Docs vs code: **disagree on the product.** Official OutLayer is off-chain compute with `request_execution`. ProvenExit is a VPN-exit build registry that verifies Intel TDX quotes *on chain* and does not import OutLayer. Fulfil (and Keyturn, not in this table) is the #1100 file that actually calls OutLayer. Do not treat ProvenExit as an OutLayer client.

### 2-party key gate (Caesura)

- Official docs (accounts the gate uses): [access keys](https://docs.near.org/protocol/accounts-contracts/access-keys.md). Seat inference, when enabled: [private inference](https://docs.near.ai/cloud/private-inference.md) and [GET attestation report](https://docs.near.ai/api-reference/attestation/get-attestation-report.md). There is no official "Caesura" page; this is a hackathon pattern on top of function-call keys.
- 5-minute testnet demo (outline): `npm install && npm test`, then `seats/round.mjs --task tasks/poisoned-page.json --driver stub --chain off` (pass = assayer refuses a poisoned drain; fail = proposer-only must not execute). Optional: one testnet verify of a sealed bundle with `--rpc testnet`.
- Docs vs code: **no official gate API to disagree with.** The word "intent" in the contract tests (`intent mismatch`) is a verdict reason, not NEAR Intents. johnservil/sigil was the wrong repo; this plan uses mitchuski/caesura only. Carry `NOTICE`.

### Escrow (Fulfil + Pinky)

- Official docs: no first-party "escrow kit" page showed up in [docs.near.org/llms.txt](https://docs.near.org/llms.txt) on this pass (same gap the 16:54Z scan noted). Related: Intents [verifier contract](https://docs.near-intents.org/integration/verifier-contract/introduction.md) and [OutLayer](https://docs.near.org/primitives/off-chain-compute/outlayer.md) for Fulfil's release path.
- 5-minute testnet demo (outline): prefer a local or testnet sandbox create + refuse/expire (pass = funds stay locked; fail = a denied destination or a bad proof does not pay). Pinky and Fulfil READMEs describe mainnet deployments; the xray demo stays on testnet and uses no mainnet funds.
- Docs vs code: **no official escrow kit to match.** Pinky *denies* withdrawals to `intents.near` (line 123); Fulfil *holds* funds as NEP-245 balances inside an `intents_contract`. They complement each other; they do not call Intents the same way.

### Scoped function-call key (nearswaps)

- Official docs: [access keys](https://docs.near.org/protocol/accounts-contracts/access-keys.md).
- 5-minute testnet demo (outline): `check_key` on a fixture key (pass = methods are exactly `trade, withdraw, recover_trade`; fail = a full-access key is refused). Then `preview_trade` with no send.
- Docs vs code: **match on the access-key model.** The allowed contract is hard-coded to `nekoorders.near`. A generic xray kit must parameterize the receiver and method list, not ship that venue as the only option. NEAR AI Cloud as a policy model is in the nearswaps README, not in `keys.ts`.

### Pre-sign MCP (Bitlens)

- Official docs: none as a NEAR primitive. Closest background is [access keys](https://docs.near.org/protocol/accounts-contracts/access-keys.md) and [smart contract testing](https://docs.near.org/smart-contracts/testing/integration-test.md). BitLens attacks run in a *local* simulator and only make RPC view calls.
- 5-minute testnet / local demo (outline): `check_transaction` against a known demo contract (pass = allow or confirm with reasons; fail = block a dangerous method + attached deposit). Nothing is signed or sent.
- Docs vs code: **no official pre-sign API.** NEAR AI Cloud appears in this file only as an optional LLM for `run_custom_attack`, not as TEE attestation. The kit is the MCP tool, not a cloud attest path.

### Front end (gap)

- Official docs: [wallet login](https://docs.near.org/web3-apps/tutorials/wallet-login.md), [NEAR Auth / passkeys](https://docs.near.org/web3-apps/tutorials/near-auth.md), [Wallet Connector (near-connect)](https://docs.near.org/tools/near-connect.md), [Social / SocialDB](https://docs.near.org/primitives/social.md). I did not find a current **web4** page in [docs.near.org/llms.txt](https://docs.near.org/llms.txt) on this pass (unverified / possible docs move).
- Docs vs code: **gap confirmed.** No shortlisted repo implements wallet selector, BOS, or web4. Hasp and Intents Checkout are 1Click payment UIs; they belong under Intents, not this layer.

### xray vault + caps (none needed)

- No official NEAR docs required for this row. No #1100 file. No new kit. Optional later reference: Veto `contract/src/lib.rs` `spend()` and Allowance `src/lib.rs` `pay()`, already covered in the reuse report, stay off this table unless forge opens a NEAR cap kit.

## Factory recipe

One shape for every kit above, taken from how xray already ships kits, packs, and MCP servers. Do not invent a new top-level `packs/` tree; there is not one in this repo today.

| Recipe part | What every kit ships | Existing xray path to follow |
|---|---|---|
| Folder layout | One package or `src/mcps/` server per kit, with a small TypeScript entry and, if needed, a contract crate beside it. | Powers are documented as Repertoire, Dynamo, and Clearing in [`docs-site/docs/plates/kits.md`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/docs-site/docs/plates/kits.md). A vendored kit example is [`vendor/@0xray/repertoire/`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/tree/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/vendor/@0xray/repertoire) (`README.md`, `LICENSE`, `AGENTS.md`, `SKILL.md`, `mcp-config.example.json`). Built-in MCP servers live under [`src/mcps/`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/tree/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/src/mcps). Foundry plants live under [`scripts/foundry/`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/tree/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/scripts/foundry) (`@0xray/foundry`). |
| Manifest / package face | `README.md`, `package.json`, `AGENTS.md`, `llms.txt`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `SKILLS.md`. Do not hand-bump the version. | [`docs-site/docs/plates/package-face.md`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/docs-site/docs/plates/package-face.md) |
| MCP tool contract | Each tool has a name, a short title, a description, and an input schema. A server is launched as a subprocess. | Built-in: [`.mcp.json`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/.mcp.json) plus `npx 0xray mcp <server>` in [`src/cli/index.ts`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/src/cli/index.ts) (the `mcp` command around the seven servers). Community wrap: `npx 0xray mcp-install <name>` and [`src/mcps/registry.json`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/src/mcps/registry.json), implemented in [`src/cli/commands/mcp-install.ts`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/src/cli/commands/mcp-install.ts). Host packs (grok-bot, Hermes, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Grok CLI, Cursor) are listed in [`docs-site/docs/plates/host-pack.md`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/docs-site/docs/plates/host-pack.md). Repertoire's example wiring is [`vendor/@0xray/repertoire/mcp-config.example.json`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/vendor/@0xray/repertoire/mcp-config.example.json). |
| Install line | One line that adds the MCP tool or provider. Proposed first-party form: `npx 0xray mcp <kit-name>` after wear has written `.mcp.json`. | Wear / MCP setup is described in [`docs-site/docs/architecture/v4-foundry.md`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/docs-site/docs/architecture/v4-foundry.md) and [`docs-site/docs/plates/consumer-mcp.md`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/docs-site/docs/plates/consumer-mcp.md). Foundry release is [`scripts/foundry/release.mjs`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/scripts/foundry/release.mjs). |
| Testnet demo | Five minutes, pass and fail, testnet or local only, no mainnet funds. | Per-kit outlines above. Premise: a newb bot can run the demo from shipped artifacts only. |
| Docs page | What it is, when you need it, official NEAR URL, the #1100 start file, and any docs-vs-code flag. Later: one "build an AI agent on NEAR with xray" guide that links the layer pages. | New pages would sit with the other plates under `docs-site/docs/`, which is the live docs tree in `v4-foundry.md`. |
| License / NOTICE carry | MIT or Apache-2.0 only. Copy the upstream LICENSE. If a NOTICE or third-party notice file exists, ship it. | Caesura: Apache-2.0 + `NOTICE`. Abalone: MIT + `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. near-sandbox is GPL and is for local testing only — do not pack it ([sandbox testing](https://docs.near.org/smart-contracts/testing/integration-test.md)). |
| Critic gate before any port | No #1100 code is copied into xray until forge sets RACI and critic passes. | Gate skill: [`grok-bot/skills/ship-ready-mill-gate/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/grok-bot/skills/ship-ready-mill-gate/SKILL.md). Foundry gate script: [`scripts/foundry/release-gate.mjs`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/scripts/foundry/release-gate.mjs). |
| Cold test of the packed tarball | `npm pack --dry-run` must contain the kit's runtime files (MCP entry, docs, LICENSE / NOTICE) before ship. | [`scripts/foundry/assert-packed-dist-cli.mjs`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/scripts/foundry/assert-packed-dist-cli.mjs) (hooked from `package.json` as `prepack` / `assert:packed-dist`). File-list pattern: [`src/__tests__/unit/wear-pack-file-list.test.ts`](https://github.com/0xRayAI/xray/blob/nibbler/near-hackathon-catalog/src/__tests__/unit/wear-pack-file-list.test.ts). Add each new kit path to a similar assert. |

Build order from the premise, still valid: Intents + x402 first, then Chain Signatures (Base path), then NEAR AI TEE, then the Caesura two-party gate. Escrow, trading key, and pre-sign can follow. Front end stays docs-only until a base exists. Spending caps stay on the shipped xray vault.

## Open questions for near and forge

1. Front end is a real gap in #1100. Can near confirm official wallet-selector / BOS / web4 URLs? I found wallet login, near-connect, and Social in `docs.near.org/llms.txt` this pass, but not web4.
2. The working table names ProvenExit for "OutLayer / TDX", but ProvenExit does not call OutLayer. Should the first worker-proof kit start from ProvenExit's on-chain TDX registry, Fulfil's `request_execution`, or both as two tools?
3. HyperNear signs Hyperliquid, not Base. Is the first Chain Signatures demo a testnet MPC `sign` only, or do we wait for a Base-payload path before calling the kit done?
4. Spending caps are "none needed." Should Veto / Allowance stay reference-only, or is a later NEAR-side cap kit still wanted?
5. x402 has no first-party page in `docs.near.org/llms.txt` this pass. Does near want the kit to cite x402.org plus Anyfare, or a NEAR-specific doc when one exists?
6. Where should new kit packages live? There is no `packs/` tree today. The closest existing homes are `src/mcps/` (first-party servers) and a vendored or npm package like `vendor/@0xray/repertoire`.
7. Official Shade Agents (`@neardefi/shade-agent-js`) are unaudited, per the 16:54Z scan. Docs-only until critic says otherwise, or a later wrap?
8. Confidential Intents (private shard) had no #1100 call site in this light read. Later pack, or fold a docs flag into the Intents kit?
9. After hackathon winners land (by 2026-11-18 5:59 PM CT, per the 16:54Z scan), should we re-check these start files before any port?

Nothing from these repos is copied into xray until forge sets RACI and critic gates it.
